info.title: Sourcery API
info.description: Public REST API for security scanning. Authenticate with an API key issued from the Sourcery dashboard.

patch.description: Update `status` and/or `severity_override` on a list of groups. At least one of the two must be provided. Setting `status` applies to every issue in each group. Setting `status` to `SNOOZED` requires `snoozed_until` (ISO-8601 UTC); other target statuses must omit `snoozed_until`. `SOLVED` is excluded from the request enum because the scanner sets it automatically — but issues currently in `SOLVED` can still be transitioned to other statuses. The response splits inputs into `updated_ids` (groups with at least one modified issue) and `failed` (with a reason per id).

get.summary: Aggregate counts across security issue groups
get.description: Returns counts of groups bucketed by status and severity, scoped to the authenticated account. A group counts toward each status bucket if any of its issues are in that status.

get.summary: Fetch a single security issue group
get.description: Returns the group with its member issues. `404 not_found` if the id doesn't exist or belongs to another account.

patch.description: Update `status` and/or `severity_override` on a list of issues. At least one of the two must be provided. Setting `status` to `SNOOZED` requires `snoozed_until` (ISO-8601 UTC); other target statuses must omit `snoozed_until`. `SOLVED` is excluded from the request enum because the scanner sets it automatically when a scan no longer detects the issue — but issues currently in `SOLVED` can still be transitioned to other statuses (e.g. to permanently `IGNORED`). ApiErrorType.title: ApiErrorType
ApiErrorType.description:
Categories of error returned in the Stripe-style envelope.

Customers branch on `error.type` for retry / alerting / surfacing
behaviour. Mirrors the (small) set of error families Stripe uses so
SDK consumers get exhaustive switch coverage without inventing custom
discriminators per status code.

BulkUpdateGroupsResponse.title: BulkUpdateGroupsResponse
BulkUpdateGroupsResponse.description:
Result of a bulk update.

`updated_ids` lists groups where at least one issue was modified.
`failed` covers every other input id with a reason — `not_found`
(unknown id or another account's id, deliberately collapsed) or
`not_eligible` (every issue in the group is already in the target state).

BulkUpdateIssuesResponse.title: BulkUpdateIssuesResponse
BulkUpdateIssuesResponse.description:
Result of a bulk update.

`updated_ids` lists the issues that were modified. `failed` covers every
other input id with a reason — `not_found` (unknown id or another
account's id, deliberately collapsed) or `not_eligible` (already in the
target state, or `SOLVED` and immutable).

DependencyGraphResponse.title: DependencyGraphResponse
DependencyGraphResponse.description:
Resolved dependency graph for a `DEPENDENCY` issue.

The chain from a project's root package to the vulnerable dependency.
`null` for non-dependency findings or when the scanner couldn't resolve
the graph.

vulnerable.title: Vulnerable
vulnerable.description: True if this node is the vulnerable package being reported.

DependencyNodeResponse.title: DependencyNodeResponse
DependencyNodeResponse.description: A package in the dependency graph for a vulnerable dependency.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Stripe-style error envelope returned for every non-2xx response.

FailedUpdate.title: FailedUpdate
FailedUpdate.description:
An id from a bulk PATCH input that did not get updated.

`not_found` covers ids that don't exist or belong to another account
(the two are deliberately collapsed to avoid leaking existence across
tenants). `not_eligible` covers ids that exist within the account but
didn't transition — most commonly because the request was a no-op
(e.g. PATCHing an already-`ACTIVE` issue to `ACTIVE`). PATCHes to
`IGNORED` / `SNOOZED` are idempotent and always land in `updated_ids`,
even when the issue is already in that state.

FailedUpdateReason.title: FailedUpdateReason
FailedUpdateReason.description: Why a particular id wasn't updated by a bulk PATCH.

IssueCounts.title: IssueCounts
IssueCounts.description:
Per-status issue counts within a group.

Field names match the ``*_count`` suffix used on top-level
``SecurityStats`` for consistency.

IssueTrackerTaskSummary.title: IssueTrackerTaskSummary
IssueTrackerTaskSummary.description: The external tracker task linked to a security issue group.

title.title: Title
title.description: Best human-readable title for the group. The scanner's group title where available; falls back to the package name (`DEPENDENCY`/`LICENSE`) or the first issue's title.

rule_id.title: Rule Id
rule_id.description: Rule identifier shared by every issue in the group. Same value as `rule_id` on the contained issues.

documentation_url.title: Documentation Url
documentation_url.description: Public catalog URL for the rule (matches `documentation_url` on each issue). See ``SecurityIssueResponse.documentation_url`` for which scanners populate this.

package_name.title: Package Name
package_name.description: Vulnerable package for `DEPENDENCY` / `LICENSE` groups; `null` for SAST / IAC / SECRET.

package_type.title: Package Type
package_type.description: Ecosystem of the package (e.g. `npm`, `pypi`, `go`); group-invariant for DEPENDENCY/LICENSE.

package_licenses.title: Package Licenses
package_licenses.description: Licenses detected for the package (LICENSE groups).

severity.description: Highest effective severity across the group's active issues.

SecurityIssueGroupDetailResponse.title: SecurityIssueGroupDetailResponse
SecurityIssueGroupDetailResponse.description:
Group with the full ``SecurityIssueResponse`` for each member issue.

Lets a coding agent walk a group's issues without re-fetching each one.

title.title: Title
title.description: Best human-readable title for the group. The scanner's group title where available; falls back to the package name (`DEPENDENCY`/`LICENSE`) or the first issue's title.

rule_id.title: Rule Id
rule_id.description: Rule identifier shared by every issue in the group. Same value as `rule_id` on the contained issues.

documentation_url.title: Documentation Url
documentation_url.description: Public catalog URL for the rule (matches `documentation_url` on each issue). See ``SecurityIssueResponse.documentation_url`` for which scanners populate this.

package_name.title: Package Name
package_name.description: Vulnerable package for `DEPENDENCY` / `LICENSE` groups; `null` for SAST / IAC / SECRET.

package_type.title: Package Type
package_type.description: Ecosystem of the package (e.g. `npm`, `pypi`, `go`); group-invariant for DEPENDENCY/LICENSE.

package_licenses.title: Package Licenses
package_licenses.description: Licenses detected for the package (LICENSE groups).

severity.description: Highest effective severity across the group's active issues.

SecurityIssueGroupResponse.title: SecurityIssueGroupResponse
SecurityIssueGroupResponse.description: A collection of related security issues — same rule, same package, etc.

issue_group_id.title: Issue Group Id
issue_group_id.description: The group this issue belongs to (same rule, same package, etc.).

rule_id.title: Rule Id
rule_id.description: Identifier of the rule or finding from the upstream scanner. For `DEPENDENCY` findings this is the CVE or GHSA id; for `SAST` / `IAC` / `SECRET` it's the scanner-emitted rule id. Stability is bounded by the upstream scanner — we pass through what the scanner produces.

documentation_url.title: Documentation Url
documentation_url.description: Public catalog URL for the rule. Populated for `DEPENDENCY` findings (NVD / GitHub Advisories); `null` otherwise — OpenGrep / Checkov / BetterLeaks don't have a stable per-rule URL convention. NVD URLs may return `403` for non-browser user agents; prefer the GHSA URL when both ids are available.

file_path.title: File Path
file_path.description: Path the scanner flagged. For DEPENDENCY findings this is the lockfile — see `manifest_file_path` for the manifest a fix should edit.

commit_sha.title: Commit Sha
commit_sha.description: Git commit at which the issue was last seen.

source_code.title: Source Code
source_code.description: Source snippet flagged by the scanner. The first line of the snippet is `source_code_line_start` (1-based, in the file).

source_code_line_start.title: Source Code Line Start
source_code_line_start.description: 1-based line number of the snippet's first line in the file.

package_licenses.title: Package Licenses
package_licenses.description: Licenses detected for the package (LICENSE findings).

fixed_versions.title: Fixed Versions
fixed_versions.description: Versions that resolve the vulnerability — typically one per release track (e.g. `["5.3.5", "4.5.4"]` for backports). Pick the version on the same major/minor track as `package_version`.

manifest_file_path.title: Manifest File Path
manifest_file_path.description: Manifest a fix should edit (e.g. `package.json` for a `package-lock.json` finding). `null` when no convention applies.

severity.description: Effective severity — `severity_override` if set, otherwise the scanner's reported severity.

original_severity.description: The scanner's reported severity, ignoring any override.

SecurityIssueResponse.title: SecurityIssueResponse
SecurityIssueResponse.description: A single finding produced by a security scan.

SecurityIssueTypeName.title: SecurityIssueTypeName
SecurityIssueTypeName.description: Category of finding the scanner produced.

total_count.title: Total Count
total_count.description: All issues regardless of status (active + snoozed + ignored + solved).

snoozed_recently_count.title: Snoozed Recently Count
snoozed_recently_count.description: Subset of the corresponding count whose status changed within the last 7 days.

ignored_recently_count.title: Ignored Recently Count
ignored_recently_count.description: Subset of the corresponding count whose status changed within the last 7 days.

solved_recently_count.title: Solved Recently Count
solved_recently_count.description: Subset of the corresponding count whose status changed within the last 7 days.

low_count.title: Low Count
low_count.description: Active issues at LOW or NO_RISK severity (post-override).

SecurityStats.title: SecurityStats
SecurityStats.description:
Aggregate counts of security issues by status and severity.

`total_count` equals `active_count + snoozed_count + ignored_count +
solved_count`. The severity counts (`critical_count` … `low_count`) are
scoped to **active** issues only and sum to `active_count`.

SecurityStatusInput.title: SecurityStatusInput
SecurityStatusInput.description:
Status a customer can transition an issue to via PATCH.

`SOLVED` is deliberately excluded — issues become `SOLVED` automatically
when the next scan no longer detects them. Setting it manually is a no-op.
